newsitem.title: UK: RUGBY UNION-WELSH INSPIRATION WOOLLER DIES IN HOSPITAL.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-WELSH INSPIRATION WOOLLER DIES IN HOSPITAL.

text.p: Wilfred Wooller, the inspiration behind epic Welsh triumphs in both their national winter and summer games, has died in hospital at the age of 85.
Wooller made sporting history the Saturday before Christmas, 1935, when Wales hosted the New Zealand All Blacks on a frozen Cardiff Arms Park.
Wales were down to 14 men in the era before replacements were allowed and trailing 12-10, when centre Wooller surged through the All Black defence.

With no one in support, he tried a short punt over the full-back's head, slipped on the straw littering the field but then heard a tremendous roar as Arthur Rees-Jones followed up for the decisive score.
Fourteen years later, after spending time as a prisoner of war, Wooller captained Glamorgan to an equally unlikely county cricket championship.
Wooller instructed his bowlers to bowl at the leg stump and formed an integral part of a leg-side field who took 120 catches.
After retiring he served as an England cricket selector and later was a blunt and outspoken journalist.
Former England cricket all-rounder Trevor Bailey paid tribute to Wooller, saying: "He was a fine rugby player, his knees came up to his thighs which made him difficult to tackle.
"He was also a tremendous cricketer and the kind of man who never had a cross word for anybody."
